instructions: Heat the broiler with a rack about 5 inches below it, and line a small sheet pan with foil.
Cut the 4 tomatoes in half and lay them on the pan cut side down. Peel the onion, cut it in half and put one half on the pan. Add the 2 garlic cloves, still in their skins.
Broil for 3 to 4 minutes, until the tops are charred in spots. Turn everything over with tongs and broil the other side for 3 to 4 minutes.
Peel the garlic. Put the tomatoes, the onion half and the garlic in a blender and blend until mostly smooth, with a little texture left.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium. Pour in the sauce. Stand back a little. It will spatter.
Stir in the 1/2 tsp cumin, the 1/2 tsp oregano and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Let it simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens a little and turns a deeper red.
Meanwhile, put the refried beans in a small pot with a splash of water over medium low. Stir now and then for about 5 minutes, until they're hot and easy to spread, then turn the heat to low.
Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro and stir it into the sauce off the heat. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat. Set it back on the lowest heat.
Slice the avocado and crumble the cotija. Pick a small handful of cilantro leaves. Seed and thinly slice the jalapeño and put it in a small bowl for the table.

Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Cook the 8 tortillas 2 or 3 at a time for about 30 seconds a side, until they puff a little and the edges turn crisp. Move them to a plate lined with paper towels.
Put 2 tortillas on each plate and spread the warm beans over them.

Add the last 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet, still over medium. Crack in 4 of the eggs and sprinkle them with 1/8 tsp of the salt and a little pepper. Cook for about 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny. If the tops of the whites still look clear, cover the pan for the last minute.
Slide one egg onto each bean-topped tortilla. Fry the other 4 eggs the same way with the last 1/8 tsp salt and a little more pepper, and add them to the plates.
Spoon the ranchero sauce over the eggs and scatter the cotija, avocado and cilantro leaves on top.
Serve hot, with the sliced jalapeño on the side.
method_notes: All three versions put a fried egg on a lightly crisped corn tortilla over warm refried beans and top it with a tomato sauce, avocado and cilantro. Downshiftology, the lead, crisps each tortilla in oil for 30 seconds a side, fries the eggs in the same pan and makes its ranchero sauce from tomatoes, onion, jalapeño and garlic charred under the broiler, blended and simmered with cumin and oregano. Love and Lemons cooks its sauce from chopped tomato with a chipotle and adds pico de gallo, and Good Cheap Eats uses enchilada sauce with two tortillas and two eggs a person. This one follows the lead's charred sauce, gives everyone two eggs and keeps the jalapeño on the side.
